clue.text: Match put to second curtain holder

parts.note: to match two scores is to tie them
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone tells a decorator to pair a match with a second curtain fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tieback is a loop or cord that holds an open curtain to the side of a window.

clue.text: Man taken in by politician's speculation

indicators.note: something taken in by a word is held inside it, so the man goes into the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
a man is a he

explanation.surface: A man is duped by a politician's speculative scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a speculative idea or hypothesis not yet proved.

clue.text: "Peers" bats squeal

indicators.note: bats in the informal sense of crazy, so the letters of the next word go wild

explanation.surface: A newspaper-style headline: bats squeal at members of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers are people of equal standing, one's equals, as in being judged by a jury of peers.

clue.text: Removal of member from a redcap university rubbish club not right

parts.note: a redcap is a British military policeman, an MP
tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following letter out of the club

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A soldier is expelled from a university's dreadful club for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAP is British slang for a military policeman. 'not right' drops R from IRON, leaving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An amputation is the surgical cutting off of a limb, a member of the body.

clue.text: Russian city pen with different top — very

indicators.note: a new first letter replaces the old one in the word for pen

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A pen with a changed cap is described as very Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with different top' swaps the B of BIRO for K, giving KIRO; the clue leaves the new letter for the solver to find from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirov is a city in European Russia, on the Vyatka river, named after a Soviet official.

clue.text: He commonly 2 26 27: a formulaic account of this acceleration run-off

definitions.text: He commonly 2 26 27: a formulaic account of this

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Einstein's equation, said with a dropped aitch, describes a runaway acceleration.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the cross-references: 'He commonly' is 'E (a Cockney dropped H), then EQUALS, EMCEE (MC) and SQUARED give E = MC squared, the formula for the energy released in this process.
explanation.definitionFit: E = mc² gives the energy released when mass is converted, as happens when atomic nuclei split or fuse.

clue.text: Casual inaction restricts a plant

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the anagram encloses the single letter
casual as in haphazard, so the letters of inaction are arranged loosely

explanation.surface: Laid-back idleness holds back a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual' rearranges INACTION to NICOTINA, and 'restricts' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the tobacco plant genus, grown in gardens for its scented flowers.

clue.text: I say large is fine by me

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise, like I say
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Someone declares that being large is perfectly acceptable to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is cool means it is acceptable to you, informal approval.

clue.text: Energy positive: head off for viewers' protection

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
a positive answer is yes

indicators.note: off in the sense of disordered, so the letters of head are jumbled

explanation.surface: A motivational slogan: stay energetic and positive, even with your head knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a beheading, removing H; in fact 'off' rearranges HEAD into HADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor shielding the eyes, protection for those who view things.

clue.text: See 5 across
Internet joke supply?

parts.note: E as in e-mail and e-commerce stands for electronic, the internet
a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: A question whether there is a supply of online jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to supply them with what they need.

clue.text: After end of war, pressure in cooker fixed by a Tommy?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
in places pressure inside the jumbled cooker
something fixed has been altered or rigged, so the letters of cooker are rearranged

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: After the war, a soldier fixes a pressure cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just says what follows the R of war. 'fixed' rearranges COOKER to OCKOER, P goes inside, then A. Tommy, by the Who, is the classic example of the genre; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is the Who's 1969 album telling a story through songs, the best-known example of the genre.

clue.text: Energy put into revamped Trivial Pursuit sadly ends in well-known 1 down

indicators.note: the energy symbol goes inside the rearranged word
revamped means remade, so the letters of trivial are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: the ends of the two following words are their last letters

explanation.surface: Someone adds energy to a revamped board game, but it ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges TRIVIAL to RLATIVI, 'put into' inserts E to make RELATIVI, and the last letters of Pursuit and sadly add T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's relativity is perhaps the most famous scientific theory, the cross-referenced 1 down.

clue.text: See 21
Novel writer Verne dismissing western as "profane"

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order
dismissing sends one letter away from the word writer

explanation.surface: The French novelist dismissed westerns as profane literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing western' takes W from WRITER, leaving RITER; 'Novel' rearranges RITER and VERNE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means showing a lack of respect for sacred things, which is what profane means.

clue.text: Roger's information received via this system

definitions.text: Roger's information received via this system

parts.words: Roger's information received via this system
parts.note: in radio-speak Roger means message received, and the device both sends and receives speech

explanation.surface: A man named Roger gets his news through some network.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a person's name; in radio procedure it means 'message received and understood', used on two-way sets such as walkie-talkies.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-way radio both transmits and receives, the set over which operators say Roger.

clue.text: Pistol faced with Big Bertha would be so overwhelmed?

definitions.text: Pistol faced with Big Bertha would be so overwhelmed?

parts.words: Pistol faced with Big Bertha would be so overwhelmed?
parts.note: a handgun against a giant artillery piece would be beaten by superior firepower, read literally

explanation.surface: A small handgun facing a huge siege cannon would be hopelessly outmatched.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha was a huge German howitzer of the First World War; the general word for being beaten is taken literally as having the smaller gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten by an opponent's superior weaponry, or more generally overwhelmed, is the sense intended.

clue.text: Ornamental edging as found on dinner plates?

definitions.meaning: a series of curved decorative curves along a border
shellfish served as food, that may be eaten from plates

explanation.surface: Decorative trim of the kind seen on crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fancy rim on china; the second sense is the shellfish on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfish of that name are eaten, and their wavy shell shape names a wavy decorative border.

clue.text: Good money gets cur drunk (superior drink?)

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters of cur are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dog given good money gets drunk on something posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand cru is a top-rated vineyard or the fine wine it produces.

clue.text: So off-the-back-of-a-lorry bargains not quite appropriate here?

definitions.text: So off-the-back-of-a-lorry bargains not quite appropriate here?

parts.words: So off-the-back-of-a-lorry bargains not quite appropriate here?
parts.note: goods sold from the rear of a vehicle, though a car rather than a lorry, hence not quite

explanation.surface: Dodgy goods sold cheaply at some event where they don't quite fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the back of a lorry' is British slang for stolen goods; here goods really are sold from the back of a vehicle, but a car's boot (trunk) rather than a lorry (truck).
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a British market where people sell unwanted goods from their car boots.

clue.text: Mineral water ultimately put in impure zinc when oxygenated

indicators.note: the end of water is placed inside the jumbled letters
impure means not in its proper state, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: oxygenated adds O, the symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Water ends up in impure zinc after it is oxygenated, a chemistry lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impure' rearranges ZINC plus O into ZICON, and 'put in' places R, the end of water, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Zircon is a zirconium silicate mineral, used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Three for the hero of century taking ring from other heroes?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

indicators.note: other means different, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
taking away one letter from the following word
from names the word the letter is taken out of

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: A centurion takes a ring from fellow heroes while the crowd applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three for the hero' is the definition: three cheers. 'taking ring from' together removes the O, and 'other' signals the anagram of what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Three cheers are traditionally called for a hero, three rounds of hurrahs.

clue.text: Pines burning? Little chance of that

parts.note: to pine is to ... or yearn
burning means very hot

explanation.surface: A pine forest catching fire is described as unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like trees, but it is the verb: longs for.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a bet or attempt with only a slim chance of success.

clue.text: Main inhabitant's lidless coal store placed at angle

indicators.note: without a lid means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a coal scuttle is a bucket for storing coal by the fire
to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Someone's coal bucket without a lid is placed at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is old poetic English for the sea. 'lidless' takes the top S off SCUTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish is a sea-dwelling mollusc, an inhabitant of the main, or ocean.

clue.text: Way after test date

indicators.note: after puts the road abbreviation behind the test

parts.note: to try something is to test it
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A road goes after an exam date.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic meeting, a date between lovers.

clue.text: Spike's football side not Southend

indicators.note: not says the following letter is taken away from the team

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
read as south end, S being the abbreviation for south and also the end of the team name

explanation.surface: Someone's football team is not Southend United.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend United is an English football club; read here as 'South end', giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a spike worn on a rider's heel, or any projecting spike.

clue.text: Hitler activity: sacking any CO without a certain bra capacity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters surround the cup
sacking as plundering throws the letters into disorder

parts.note: a C cup is one particular bra size

explanation.surface: Hitler sacks any commanding officer who lacks a certain bra size.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitler's activity is meant as occupying other countries. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and a C cup is a bra size.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupancy here means occupation of territory, the German taking over of neighbouring countries.

clue.text: Switched old body with Brummie presenter

indicators.note: switched round, so the old organisation together with the setter is read back to front

parts.note: the EEC, the European Economic Community, was a former body
Brummie is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A Birmingham native swaps places with an outdated organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie, the setter's pseudonym (also slang for someone from Birmingham), stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, someone who presents a show.

clue.text: Checked and balanced

definitions.meaning: marked with a pattern of squares, like a chessboard
evened up, as when accounts are settled

explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of squares is checked, and settling up accounts makes them even and settled.

clue.text: star@earth.net finally reversed disease

indicators.note: reversed means the whole assembled run is read backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a star
the @ symbol is read as at
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

explanation.surface: An email address of a celebrity is said to be a disease when reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: The email address is read piece by piece: star, at, earth and the last letter of net, all turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, often called lockjaw.
